scoring_justification: Recomputing Tc and λ from the submitted Eliashberg function α²F(ω) and comparing to the paper's reported Tc and λ range provides the strongest verification.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference superconducting critical temperature (Tc) and electron-phonon coupling constant (λ) range for FCC metallic hydrogen at r_s=1.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: 'The numerical solution of the Eliashberg equation ... gives the very high value of T_c ≈ 600 K' and 'The coupling constant λ ... has the very large value λ ≈ 7.'
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's own reported results; no external dataset required.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's actual reported numbers used for comparison.

outputs.description: The Eliashberg spectral function α²F(ω) for FCC metallic hydrogen at r_s=1. The checker will numerically integrate this function to obtain the electron-phonon coupling constant λ, the logarithmic average frequency ω_log, and the resulting Tc via the McMillan-Allen-Dynes formula.

schema.description: Single line with the superconducting critical temperature in Kelvin, computed from the submitted α²F using the McMillan-Allen-Dynes formula with μ*=0.1.

outputs.description: The agent's reported Tc value. The checker compares this value directly to the paper's reported Tc (hidden) within a tolerance band, as a secondary check in addition to the recomputed Tc from the α²F data.

output_contract.notes: Primary scoring is based on the Tc recomputed by the checker from the submitted α²F, with sanity checks on λ. The agent's directly submitted Tc is also compared as a supporting reference. The lattice stability calculations of the original paper are excluded per the task scope.

steps.description: Recompute Tc and λ from the α²F CSV, compare Tc to paper gold, and sanity-check λ.
Compare the agent's directly reported Tc to the paper's reported Tc within tolerance.
